nodes.name: Characteristic function
nodes.statement: Let $\mu$ be a measure on a real inner product space $E$. The characteristic function of $\mu$, denoted by $\hat{\mu}$, is the function $E \to \mathbb{C}$ defined by \begin{align*} \hat{\mu}(t) = \int_x e^{i \langle t, x \rangle} d\mu(x) \: . \end{align*} The characteristic function of a random variable $X$ is defined as the characteristic function of $\mathcal L(X)$.
nodes.label: def:charFun

nodes.statement: For all $t$, $\Vert\hat{\mu}(t)\Vert \le 1$.
nodes.label: lem:charFun_bounded

nodes.statement: If $\mu[|X|^n] < \infty$ then the characteristic function of $\mu$ is continuously differentiable of order $n$.
nodes.label: lem:charFun_contDiff

nodes.statement: The characteristic function is a continuous function.
nodes.label: lem:charFun_continuous

nodes.statement: $\hat{\mu}(-t) = \overline{\hat{\mu}(t)}$.
nodes.label: lem:charFun_neg

nodes.statement: For $a \in \mathbb{R}$ and $X$ a random variable with law $\mu$, the characteristic function of $a X$ is $t \mapsto \hat{\mu}(at)$.
nodes.label: lem:charFun_smul

nodes.statement: If two random variables $X, Y : \Omega \to S$ with laws $\mu$ and $\nu$ are independent, then $X+Y$ has characteristic function $\hat{\mu} \times \hat{\nu}$.
nodes.label: lem:charFun_add_of_indep

nodes.statement: \begin{align*} \int_{-r}^r e^{i t} \, d t = 2 \sin r \: . \end{align*}
nodes.label: lem:integral_exp_I

nodes.statement: \begin{align*} \int_{-r}^r \hat{\mu}(t) dt = 2 r \int \frac{\sin(r x)}{r x} \, d\mu(x) \end{align*}
nodes.label: lem:integral_charFun

nodes.statement: We will use Fubini's theorem to exchange the order of integration. \begin{align*} \int_{-r}^r \hat{\mu}(t) \, dt &= \int_{-r}^r \int e^{i t x} \, d\mu(x) \, dt \\ &= \int \left( \int_{-r}^r e^{i t x} \, dt \right) \, d\mu(x) \\ &= \int 2 \frac{\sin(r x)}{x} \, d\mu(x) \\ &= 2 r \int \frac{\sin(r x)}{r x} \, d\mu(x) \end{align*}
For $\mu$ a probability measure on $\mathbb{R}$ and $r > 0$, \begin{align*} \mu \left\{x \mid |x| > r\right\} &\le \frac{r}{2} \int_{-2/r}^{2/r} (1 - \hat{\mu}(t))dt \: . \end{align*}
nodes.label: lem:charFun_bound_large

nodes.statement: We will use Lemma~\ref{lem:integral_charFun} with $r$ replaced by $2/r$. \begin{align*} \frac{r}{2} \int_{-2/r}^{2/r} (1 - \hat{\mu}(t))dt &= 2 - \frac{r}{2} \int_{-2/r}^{2/r} \hat{\mu}(t)dt \\ &= 2 - 2 \int \frac{\sin(2 x / r)}{2 x / r} \, d\mu(x) \\ &= 2 \int \left(1 - \frac{\sin(2 x / r)}{2 x / r}\right) \, d\mu(x) \\ &\ge 2 \int_{|x| \ge r} \left(1 - \frac{\sin(2 x / r)}{2 x / r}\right) \, d\mu(x) \\ &\ge \mu\{x \mid |x| > r\} \: . \end{align*} In the end we used that $\sin x \le x /2$ for $x \ge 2$.

For $\mu$ a probability measure on an inner product space $E$ and $r > 0$, $a \in E$, \begin{align*} \mu \left\{x \mid \vert\langle a, x\rangle\vert > r\right\} &\le \frac{r}{2} \int_{-2/r}^{2/r} (1 - \hat{\mu}(t \cdot a))dt \: . \end{align*}
nodes.label: lem:charFun_bound_inner

Let $\mu, \mu_1, \mu_2, \ldots$ be probability measures on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with characteristic functions $\hat{\mu}, \hat{\mu}_1, \hat{\mu}_2, \ldots$ such that $\hat{\mu}_n \to \hat{\mu}$. Then for all exponential polynomial $f \in \mathcal M$, $\mu_n[f] \to \nu[f]$.

nodes.statement: Two finite measures on a complete separable metric space are equal iff they have the same characteristic function.
nodes.section: 1.2 Convergence of characteristic functions and weak convergence of measures
nodes.label: lem:ext_charFun

nodes.statement: See Mathlib PR \#19783. The sub-algebra $\mathcal M$ of exponential polynomials is separating by Lemma~\ref{lem:separates_points_expPoly} and~\ref{thm:separating_starSubalgebra}. Equality of characteristic functions implies equality on $\mathcal M$, which then implies equality of the measures since $\mathcal M$ is separating.
nodes.section: 1.2 Convergence of characteristic functions and weak convergence of measures

nodes.statement: Let $(\mu_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be measures on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with characteristic functions $(\hat{\mu}_n)$. If $\hat{\mu}_n$ converges pointwise to a function $f$ which is continuous at 0, then $(\mu_n)$ is tight.
nodes.section: 1.2 Convergence of characteristic functions and weak convergence of measures
nodes.label: lem:tight_of_tendsto_charFun

nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lem:charFun_bound_inner} and dominated convergence, for all $a \in \mathbb{R}^d$ and $r > 0$, \begin{align*} \lim_{n \to +\infty} \mu_n \left\{x \mid |\langle a, x\rangle| \ge r\right\} &\le \lim_{n \to +\infty} \frac{r}{2} \int_{-2/r}^{2/r} (1 - \hat{\mu}_n(\langle a, t\rangle))dt \\ &= \frac{r}{2} \int_{-2/r}^{2/r} (1 - f(\langle a, t\rangle))dt \end{align*} The right-hand side converges to 0 as $r \to +\infty$ by continuity of $f$ at 0. This shows that the family is tight.
nodes.section: 1.2 Convergence of characteristic functions and weak convergence of measures

nodes.name: Convergence of characteristic functions and weak convergence of measures
nodes.statement: Let $\mu, \mu_1, \mu_2, \ldots$ be probability measures on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with characteristic functions $\hat{\mu}, \hat{\mu}_1, \hat{\mu}_2, \ldots$. Then $\mu_n \xrightarrow{w} \mu$ iff for all $t$, $\hat{\mu}_n(t) \to \hat{\mu}(t)$.
nodes.section: 1.2 Convergence of characteristic functions and weak convergence of measures
nodes.label: thm:charFun_tendsto_iff_measure_tendsto

nodes.statement: For all $t$, $x \mapsto e^{i \langle t, x \rangle}$ is a bounded continuous function. Hence by the definition of convergence in distribution, $\mu_n \xrightarrow{w} \mu \implies \hat{\mu}_n(t) \to \hat{\mu}(t)$ for all $t$. Let's now prove the other direction. If the characteristic functions converge pointwise, we get from Lemma~\ref{lem:tight_of_tendsto_charFun} that the family of measures is tight. Then apply Lemma~\ref{lem:cvg_of_separating} to the subalgebra $\mathcal M$: it suffices to show that $\mu_n[f] \to \mu[f]$ for all $f \in \mathcal M$. This is obtained with Lemma~\ref{lem:tendsto_M_of_tendsto_charFun}.
nodes.section: 1.2 Convergence of characteristic functions and weak convergence of measures

nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a real random variable with characteristic function $\phi$ with $\mathbb{E}[\vert X \vert^n] < \infty$ and let $k \le n$. Then the $k$\textsuperscript{th} derivative of $\phi$ is $\phi^{(k)}(t) = \mathbb{E}[i X]^k e^{i t X}$ \: .

nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a real random variable with characteristic function $\phi$, with $\mathbb{E}[\vert X \vert^n] < \infty$. Then as $t \to 0$, \begin{align*} \phi(t) = \sum_{k=0}^n \frac{(it)^k \mathbb{E}[X^k]}{k!} + o(t^n) \: . \end{align*}

nodes.statement: For $t\in\mathbb{C}$, $\lim_{n\to\infty}(1+t/n+o(1/n))^n=\exp(t)$ (where the little-$o$ term may be complex).

nodes.name: Central limit theorem
nodes.statement: Let $X_1, X_2, \ldots$ be i.i.d. real random variables with mean 0 and variance 1, and let $Z$ be a random variable with law $\mathcal N(0,1)$. Then \begin{align*} \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\sum_{k=1}^n X_k \xrightarrow{d} Z \: . \end{align*}
nodes.section: 2.1 The central limit theorem for real random variables
nodes.label: thm:clt

nodes.statement: Let $S_n = \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\sum_{k=1}^n X_k$. Let $\phi$ be the characteristic function of $X_k$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:charFun_smul} and~\ref{lem:charFun_add_of_indep}, the characteristic function of $S_n$ is $\phi_n(t) = (\phi(n^{-1/2}t))^n$. By Lemma \ref{lem:charFun_taylor}, \begin{align*} \phi_n(t) = (\phi(n^{-1/2}t))^n = \left(1 - \frac{1}{2n}t^2 + o(\frac{1}{n})\right)^n \to_{n \to +\infty} e^{-t^2/2} \: . \end{align*} Since the r.h.s. is the characteristic function of $Z$, we conclude that $\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\sum_{k=1}^n X_k \xrightarrow{d} Z$ by Lemma~\ref{thm:charFun_tendsto_iff_measure_tendsto}.
nodes.section: 2.1 The central limit theorem for real random variables

nodes.name: Cramér-Wold
nodes.statement: Let $X, X_1, X_2, \ldots$ be random variables in $\mathbb{R}^d$. Then $X_n \xrightarrow{d} X$ iff for every $a \in \mathbb{R}^d$, $\langle a, X_n \rangle \xrightarrow{d} \langle a, X \rangle$.
nodes.section: 2.2 The central limit theorem for random variables in $\mathbb{R}^d$
nodes.label: thm:cramer_wold

nodes.statement: By Theorem~\ref{thm:charFun_tendsto_iff_measure_tendsto}, the convergence in distribution of the random variables is equivalent to the convergence of their characteristic functions for each $a \in \mathbb{R}^d$, which for each such $a$ is equivalent to the convergence in distribution of the random variables $\langle a, X_n \rangle$ by the same theorem.
nodes.section: 2.2 The central limit theorem for random variables in $\mathbb{R}^d$

nodes.name: Central limit theorem in $\mathbb{R}^d$
nodes.statement: Let $X_1, X_2, \ldots$ be i.i.d. random variables in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with mean 0 and identity covariance matrix, and let $Z$ be a random variable with law $\mathcal N(0,I_d)$. Then \begin{align*} \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\sum_{k=1}^n X_k \xrightarrow{d} Z \: . \end{align*}
nodes.section: 2.2 The central limit theorem for random variables in $\mathbb{R}^d$
nodes.label: thm:multivariate_clt

nodes.statement: A measure on $\mathbb{R}$ is Gaussian if it is equal to $\mathcal{N}(m, \sigma^2)$ for some $m \in \mathbb{R}$ and $\sigma^2 \ge 0$, in which $\mathcal{N}(m, \sigma^2)$ is the measure absolutely continuous with respect to the Lebesgue measure with density $x \mapsto \frac{1}{\sqrt{2 \pi \sigma^2}}e^{- \frac{1}{2\sigma^2}(x - m)^2}$ if $\sigma^2>0$ and the Dirac probability measure at $m$ if $\sigma^2 = 0$.
nodes.label: def:gaussianReal

nodes.statement: A real Gaussian measure is a probability measure.
nodes.label: lem:isProbabilityMeasure_gaussianReal

nodes.statement: The Gaussian distribution $\mathcal N(m, \sigma^2)$ has characteristic function $\phi(t) = e^{itm - \sigma^2 t^2 /2}$.
nodes.label: lem:gaussian_charFun

nodes.statement: The sum of two independent real Gaussian random variables is Gaussian.
nodes.label: lem:add_gaussianReal

nodes.statement: A Borel measure $\mu$ on a separable Banach space $E$ is said to be Gaussian if for all continuous linear maps $\ell : E \to \mathbb{R}$, the pushforward $\ell_*\mu$ is a real Gaussian measure.
nodes.label: def:isGaussian

nodes.statement: A Gaussian measure is a probability measure.
nodes.label: lem:isProbabilityMeasure_isGaussian

nodes.statement: The real Gaussian measures are Gaussian measures in the sense of Definition~\ref{def:isGaussian}.
nodes.label: lem:isGaussian_gaussianReal

nodes.statement: The sum of two independent Gaussian random variables is Gaussian.
nodes.label: lem:isGaussian_add

nodes.statement: Let $E$ be a finite dimensional real inner product space and let $b_1, \ldots, b_d$ be an orthonormal basis of $E$. Let $X_1, \ldots, X_d$ be independent standard Gaussian random variables on $\mathbb{R}$. Then the law of $X_1 b_1 + \ldots + X_d b_d$ is a Gaussian measure on $E$.
nodes.label: lem:stdGaussian_finiteDimensional

nodes.name: Weak convergence of probability measures
nodes.statement: In a topological space $S$ in which the opens are measurable, we say that a sequence of probability measures $\mu_n$ converges weakly to a probability measure $\mu$ and write $\mu_n \xrightarrow{w} \mu$ if $\mu_n[f] \to \mu[f]$ for every bounded continuous function $f : S \to \mathbb{R}$.
nodes.label: def:weak_cvg_measure

nodes.name: Convergence in distribution
nodes.statement: We say that $X_n$ converges in distribution to $X$ and write $X_n \xrightarrow{d} X$ if $\mathcal L(X_n) \xrightarrow{w} \mathcal L(X)$.
nodes.label: def:cvg_distribution

nodes.statement: A set $\mathcal F$ of functions $E \to F$ separates points in $E$ if for all $x, y \in E$ with $x \ne y$, there exists $f \in \mathcal F$ with $f(x) \ne f(y)$.
nodes.label: def:separates_points

nodes.statement:
In a Borel space $E$, if two probability measures $\mu, 
u$ on $E$ are such that $\mu[f] = 
u[f]$ for all $f \in C_b(E, \mathbb{C})$, the set of bounded continuous functions from $E$ to $\mathbb{C}$, then $\mu = 
u$.
nodes.label: lem:bounded_continuous_separating

nodes.statement: The Mathlib lemma \texttt{MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.ext\_of\_forall\_lintegral\_eq} shows that the result is true for $C_b(E, \mathbb{R}_+)$. Since $C_b(E, \mathbb{R}_{+}) \subseteq C_b(E, \mathbb{C})$, we get the result.
$x \mapsto (t \mapsto \exp(i \langle t, x \rangle))$ is a monoid homomorphism from $(E,+)$ to $C_b(E, \mathbb{C})$.
nodes.label: lem:exp_character

nodes.statement: The functions of the form $x \mapsto \sum_{k=1}^n a_k e^{i\langle t_k, x\rangle}$ for $n \in \mathbb{N}$, $a_1, \ldots, a_n \in \mathbb{R}$ and $t_1, \ldots, t_n \in E$ are a star-subalgebra of $C_b(E, \mathbb{C})$.
nodes.label: lem:starSubalgebra_expPoly

nodes.statement: The monoid homomorphism can be lifted to a homomorphism of algebras from \texttt{AddMonoidAlgebra ℝ E} to $C_b(E, \mathbb{C})$ using \texttt{AddMonoidAlgebra.lift}. $\mathcal M$ is the range of this homomorphism. The ``star'' part can be checked easily.
The star-subalgebra $\mathcal M$ separates points.
nodes.label: lem:separates_points_expPoly

nodes.statement: Let $\mu$ be a finite measure on a Borel space $E$ and let $K$ be a measurable compact set such that $\mu(K^c) \le \varepsilon$. Let $f \in C(E, \mathbb{R})$. Then \begin{align*} \left\vert \mu[fe^{-\varepsilon \Vert f \Vert^2}] - \mu[f e^{-\varepsilon \Vert f \Vert^2} \mathbb{I}_K] \right\vert \le \sqrt{\varepsilon} \: . \end{align*}
nodes.label: lem:integral_restrict_compact

nodes.statement: For any $f \in C_b(E, \mathbb{R})$ and a probability measure $\mu$, \begin{align*} \mu[f] = \lim_{\varepsilon \to 0} \mu\left[f e^{-\varepsilon \Vert f \Vert^2} \right] \: . \end{align*}
nodes.label: lem:introduce_exponential

nodes.name: Subalgebras separating points
nodes.statement:
Let $E$ be a complete separable pseudo-metric space. Let $\mathcal A \subseteq C_b(E, \mathbb{C})$ be a star-subalgebra that separates points. Then if two probability measures $\mu, 
u$ of $E$ are such that $\mu[f] = 
u[f]$ for all $f \in \mathcal A$, then $\mu = 
u$.
nodes.label: thm:separating_starSubalgebra

nodes.statement:
Let $\mu$ and $
u$ be two probability measures such that $\mu[f] = 
u[f]$ for all $f \in \mathcal A$. We want to prove that $\mu = 
u$. By Lemma~ef{lem:bounded_continuous_separating}, it suffices to prove that for all $g \in C_b(E, \mathbb{C})$, $\mu[g] = 
u[g]$. This is proved in Mathlib PR \#19782.

Let $\mathcal A$ be a subalgebra of $C_b(E, \mathbb{C})$ that separates points. Let $\mu, \mu_1, \mu_2, \ldots$ be probability measures, with $(\mu_n)$ tight. If for all $f \in \mathcal A$, $\mu_n[f] \to \mu[f]$, then $\mu_n \xrightarrow{w} \mu$.
nodes.label: lem:cvg_of_separating

nodes.statement: To show convergence to $\mu$, it suffices to show that every subsequence has a subsequence that converges to $\mu$ (\texttt{Filter.tendsto\_of\_subseq\_tendsto}). Since the family is tight, it is relatively compact by Prokhorov's theorem. We get that each subsequence has a converging subsequence. Let then $\mu'$ be a weak limit of $\mu_n$. We have $\mu_n[f] \to \mu'[f]$ and $\mu_n[f] \to \mu[f]$ for all $f \in \mathcal A$, hence $\mu'[f] = \mu[f]$ for all $f \in \mathcal A$. Since $\mathcal A$ separates points, $\mathcal \mu' = \mu$ by Theorem~\ref{thm:separating_starSubalgebra}.
A set $S$ of measures on $\Omega$ is tight if for all $\varepsilon > 0$ there exists a compact set $K$ such that for all $\mu \in S$, $\mu(K^c) \le \varepsilon$.
nodes.label: def:tight

nodes.statement: Let $S$ be a set of measures on a finite-dimensional normed space $E$. Then $S$ is tight iff $\lim_{r \to +\infty}\sup_{\mu \in S} \mu\{\Vert x \Vert > r\} = 0$.
nodes.label: lem:isTightMeasureSet_iff_norm

nodes.statement: Let $S$ be a set of measures on a finite-dimensional inner product space $E$. Then $S$ is tight iff for all $y \in E$, $\lim_{r \to +\infty}\sup_{\mu \in S} \mu\{\vert\langle y, x\rangle\vert > r\} = 0$.
nodes.label: lem:isTightMeasureSet_iff_sup_inner

nodes.statement: Let $(\mu_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence of measures on a finite-dimensional inner product space $E$. Then the set $\{\mu_n \mid n \in \mathbb{N}\}$ is tight iff for all $y \in E$, $\lim_{r \to +\infty}\limsup_{n \to \infty} \mu_n\{\vert\langle y, x\rangle\vert > r\} = 0$.
nodes.label: lem:isTightMeasureSet_iff_basis

nodes.name: Prokhorov's theorem
nodes.statement: Let $E$ be a complete separable metric space and let $S \subseteq \mathcal P(E)$. Then the following are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item $S$ is tight. \item the closure of $S$ is compact. \end{enumerate}
nodes.label: thm:prokhorov

nodes.statement: Let $E$ be a metric space and let $S \subseteq \mathcal P(E)$ be tight. Then the closure of $S$ is compact.
nodes.label: lem:relatively_compact_of_tight
